# Today at UC San Diego

> UC San Diego's news and research hub covering breakthrough discoveries in biomedical innovation, public health, neurotechnology, and faculty achievements.

Today at UC San Diego showcases cutting-edge research from the university's schools of medicine, engineering, and public health, along with the Scripps Institution of Oceanography and San Diego Supercomputer Center. The site highlights faculty accomplishments, research funding awards, and innovations addressing major health challenges from cancer and rare diseases to organ transplantation and cardiovascular health.

## Key Topics

- UC San Diego research
- Biomedical innovation
- Public health
- Cardiovascular health
- AI and machine learning
- Organ transplantation
- Rare diseases
- Wearable technology
- Gene editing
- 3D bioprinting
- Neuromorphic hardware
- Cancer research
- Faculty awards
- Research funding
- Health sciences

## Biomedical Innovation & Transplantation

- [ARPA-H Project Awarded at UC San Diego Aims to End Liver Transplant Shortage with 3D Bioprinting](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/arpa-h-project-awarded-at-uc-san-diego-aims-to-end-liver-transplant-shortage-with-3d-bioprinting): UC San Diego awarded $25.8M ARPA-H grant for 3D bioprinting patient-specific livers.
- [Bold Ideas for Reimagining Organ Donation and Transplantation](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/bold-ideas-for-reimagining-organ-donation-and-transplantation): UC San Diego REIMAGINE Center addresses critical organ shortage through innovative initiatives.
- [Meet our Distinguished Alumni of the Year: Transplant Specialist Mary Moss Chandran, Pharm.D. '12](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/meet-our-distinguished-alumni-of-the-year-transplant-specialist-mary-moss-chandran-08-pharmd-1): Mary Moss Chandran honored as Distinguished Alumni of the Year for organ transplant expertise.

## AI & Advanced Computing

- [Brain-inspired Device Could Lead to Faster, More Energy-efficient AI Hardware](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/brain-inspired-device-could-lead-to-faster-more-energy-efficient-ai-hardware): UC San Diego develops neuromorphic hardware mimicking brain function for efficient AI.
- [San Diego Supercomputer Center Powers AI Model to Improve Prostate Cancer Care](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/san-diego-supercomputer-center-powers-ai-model-to-improve-prostate-cancer-care): SDSC AI model improves prostate cancer radiation therapy precision using supercomputing.
- [Rebalancing the Gut: How AI Solved a 25-Year Crohn's Disease Mystery](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/rebalancing-the-gut-how-ai-solved-a-25-year-crohns-disease-mystery): UC San Diego AI research resolves decades-long debate on Crohn's disease genetics.

## Disease Research & Genetic Innovation

- [From Rett and Pitt-Hopkins to ALS: 5 Rare Diseases UC San Diego Researchers are Tackling in the Lab](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/from-rett-and-pitt-hopkins-to-als-5-rare-diseases-uc-san-diego-researchers-are-tackling-in-the-lab): UC San Diego stem cell researchers advance treatments for five rare genetic diseases.
- [Three-Hit Model Describes the Causes of Autism](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/three-hit-model-describes-the-causes-of-autism): UC San Diego School of Medicine proposes unified biological model explaining autism causes.
- [Open Philanthropy Awards Grant for Genetic Technology Designed to Stop Malaria](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/open-philanthropy-awards-grant-for-genetic-technology-designed-to-stop-malaria): UC San Diego receives $500K grant for gene-editing technology to prevent malaria spread.
- [Cannabis Use Disorder Triples Risk of Oral Cancer](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/cannabis-use-disorder-triples-risk-of-oral-cancer): UC San Diego research links cannabis use disorder to significantly higher oral cancer risk.

## Public Health & Wearable Technology

- [Just Rise: Study Finds Frequent Standing May Boost Heart Health After Menopause](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/frequent-standing-may-boost-heart-health-after-menopause): UC San Diego study finds standing breaks may improve heart health for postmenopausal women.
- [Wristband Sensor Provides All-in-one Monitoring for Diabetes and Cardiovascular Care](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/wristband-sensor-provides-all-in-one-monitoring-for-diabetes-and-cardiovascular-care): UC San Diego wearable wristband tracks glucose and cardiovascular signals for diabetes management.
- [Understanding Substance Use Across the Full Spectrum of Sexual Identity](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/understanding-substance-use-across-the-full-spectrum-of-sexual-identity): UC San Diego analysis reveals higher substance use rates among LGBTQ+ populations.
- [Center for OB/GYN Research Innovation is Leading the Way to Improve Women's Health](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/center-for-ob-gyn-research-innovation-is-leading-the-way-to-improve-womens-health): UC San Diego Center for OB/GYN Research Innovation hosts inaugural Women's Health Symposium.
- [Spreading Drug Costs Over the Year May Ease Financial Burden for Medicare Cancer Patients](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/spreading-drug-costs-over-the-year-may-ease-financial-burden-for-medicare-cancer-patients): UC San Diego study examines Medicare payment plans to reduce cancer drug cost burden.

## Faculty Awards & Interdisciplinary Research

- [Second Cohort of UC San Diego's 2025 Convene and Influence Awardees Announced](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/second-cohort-of-uc-san-diegos-2025-convene-and-influence-awardees-announced): Six UC San Diego faculty teams selected for Fall 2025 Convene and Influence Awards.
- [From Lebanon's Vineyards to Vision Restoration](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/from-lebanons-vineyards-to-vision-restoration): UC San Diego professor Shadi Dayeh innovates in brain mapping and eye transplantation.

## Environmental & Social Research

- [Scripps Scientists in Antarctica Studying Retreating Glaciers, Cancer-Fighting Microbes and More](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/scripps-scientists-in-antarctica-studying-retreating-glaciers-cancer-fighting-microbes-and-more): Scripps Institution researchers conduct field research in Antarctica on glaciers and microbes.
- [Americans Don't Just Fear Driverless Cars Will Crash — They Fear Mass Job Losses](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/americans-dont-just-fear-driverless-cars-will-crashthey-fear-mass-job-loss): UC San Diego study reveals Americans' concerns about autonomous vehicles and job displacement.

## Optional

- [A Scholar's Journey from Cambridge to California: Uncovering UC San Diego's East Asia Collection](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/a-scholars-journey-from-cambridge-to-california-uncovering-uc-san-diegos-east-asia-collection): Cambridge PhD researcher uses UC San Diego's East Asia collection via visiting scholar program.
